lessons.title: An ACD distributes. A skill group is the Five9 queue
objectives: Separate the general word from the Five9 object
paragraphs: Wikipedia describes an automatic call distributor as a telephony device that answers and distributes incoming calls to a group of terminals or agents. It says the route can depend on the caller's number, the number dialed, the time of day, or an answer to a voice prompt, and that an advanced system may take input from CTI, CSTA, or an IVR.

The Five9 skill groups chapter is the queue this lab could read. It says skill groups organize users who have the agent or supervisor role into groups assigned to the call queues that are part of campaigns. That is the Five9 object. The Wikipedia article is the general word ACD. Do not treat them as the same paragraph.

lessons.title: A routing review you can finish
paragraphs: A routing note can be finished with the pages that opened. Say that a skill group is agent or supervisor users on a campaign queue. Say whether the user and the campaign have one group or several. Say which tab the campaign type uses. Say that service level and voicemail are topic titles.

Then stop. Availability, caller ID, ANI, IVR, and DNIS are routing inputs on the Wikipedia page, not a Five9 field list. Competency-based routing is a sentence on the quality page, in the quality chapter, not a skill-group setting this page printed.
